t: Section 13908(d)(1) is amended by striking “but shall not exceed $300”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment that removes a dollar cap from an existing statutory provision. There is no tempting participation reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 13908(d)(1) is amended by striking “but shall not exceed $300”.

opus.w: This amendment only removes a dollar cap on a fee. It sets up no consultation, coordination, comment period, hearing or advisory process with anyone outside the federal government. Other parts of section 13908 may involve States or rulemaking, but this text does not create or require any such participation.
opus.s: Section 13908(d)(1) is amended by striking “but shall not exceed $300”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 13908 of Title 49 deals with the motor carrier registration system, and other parts of it involve regulations and cooperation with the States. That could make the amendment look like it touches participation. But the definition applies to the text in front of us. This text only deletes a $300 cap on a fee. It mentions no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue, and no outside party appears at all.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statutory provision regarding a monetary limit. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, public hearings, or advisory committees. The text simply changes a number in the law, which is a legislative action, not a participatory process involving non-federal parties in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 13908(d)(1) is amended by striking “but shall not exceed $300”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute could implicitly involve public participation if the amendment itself is part of a broader rulemaking process, but the text provided is merely a technical amendment to a dollar limit. It contains no language regarding consultation, hearings, comments, or advisory bodies.
